headline: Apple challenges UK government's demand for iCloud backdoor access
summary: Apple is reportedly filing a second legal challenge against the U.K. government's demand for access to encrypted user data stored in iCloud.
details: Apple has reportedly filed a complaint with the U.K.'s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, a court that hears cases related to government surveillance.
The government had previously issued a 'technical capability notice,' a secret legal order demanding access to users' data, even if encrypted.
Critics view this as a demand for a backdoor into Apple's cloud backups, particularly those protected by Advanced Data Protection (ADP), which offers end-to-end encryption.

This marks Apple's second legal challenge on this issue, following a similar dispute in early 2025 that was reportedly dropped after U.S. intervention. Following the first order, Apple removed ADP for UK users.
The U.K. government issued a second order in October, which Apple is now contesting through this new legal action.
caption:
Apple is once again fighting the UK government over access to encrypted iCloud data, challenging a secret legal order that critics call a backdoor.

Apple has reportedly filed a complaint with the U.K.'s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, a court that hears cases related to government surveillance.

The government had previously issued a 'technical capability notice,' a secret legal order demanding access to users' data, even if encrypted.

Critics view this as a demand for a backdoor into Apple's cloud backups, particularly those protected by Advanced Data Protection (ADP), which offers end-to-end encryption.

This marks Apple's second legal challenge on this issue, following a similar dispute in early 2025 that was reportedly dropped after U.S. intervention. Following the first order, Apple removed ADP for UK users.

The U.K. government issued a second order in October, which Apple is now contesting through this new legal action.
